₹10,00,000 per month paid directly into private commercial bank fixed deposits
Free international airline travel for the athlete's family for 8 years
A one-time cash grant of ₹50,000 given at the national championship
explanation: Under the Khelo India Talent Development scheme, selected high-potential athletes receive financial assistance of ₹5 Lakh per annum for 8 years to cover training, equipment, nutrition, and medical expenses.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: According to the enacted National Anti-Doping Act (2022) text of India, what statutory power was granted to the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA India)?
options: NADA received statutory powers for testing, investigations, intelligence, and search operations
Power to select the starting eleven players for the Indian national cricket team
Authority to construct national commercial highways and international airport terminals
Authority to issue national currency notes and regulate international trade tariffs
explanation: The National Anti-Doping Act, 2022 established NADA as a statutory body with powers of investigation, intelligence, sample collection, and conducting search/seizure operations to ensure clean sports in India. This item is anchored to the enacted Act text; as of the notification date, the NADA Rules 2021 remained the operative rules.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the 2024 WADA Prohibited List, in which category are Beta-2 Agonists (e.g., Salbutamol, Formoterol) classified, and what are the permitted therapeutic inhalation thresholds?
options: Category M1; classified strictly as a mechanical manipulation of blood components
Category S1, anabolic agents, completely banned at all times in any quantity via any route
Category S6, stimulants, permitted only during international flight travel
Beta-2 agonists are S3; inhaled salbutamol is allowed within specified dose limits
explanation: Under WADA S3, inhaled salbutamol is permitted for asthma management up to max 1,600 mcg/24h (max 600 mcg per 8h) without a TUE. Exceeding these limits is considered an Adverse Analytical Finding.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: In the Anti-Doping Athlete Biological Passport (ABP) module, what physiological markers are tracked longitudinally in the 'Hematological Module'?
options: A lipid module tracks cholesterol, triglycerides, and other blood fats
It tracks hemoglobin, hematocrit, reticulocytes, and the OFF-score
A renal module tracks creatinine, urea, and kidney filtration markers
A metabolic module tracks glucose, urine pH, and hydration markers
explanation: The haematological Athlete Biological Passport module tracks haemoglobin, haematocrit, reticulocytes, and calculated indices such as the OFF-score.

topic: Olympic, Asian and Paralympic major competitions
subtopic: International games, venues and Olympic governance
text: Which Japanese prefecture and city will host the XX Asian Games in the year 2026?
options: Hokkaido Prefecture and Sapporo City, Japan
Aichi-Nagoya will host the Asian Games
Tokyo Metropolitan Area, Japan
Osaka Prefecture and Kyoto City, Japan
explanation: The 20th Asian Games in 2026 will be co-hosted by Aichi Prefecture and its capital city Nagoya, Japan (Aichi-Nagoya 2026).

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Sports Authority of India and national schemes
text: What is the primary objective of the 'National Sports Development Fund' (NSDF) instituted by the Government of India?
options: The NSDF supports elite athletes, coaching, facilities, and customized training
Funding private commercial real estate investments for sports federation officials
Paying pensions exclusively to retired international sports commentators
Purchasing international television broadcasting rights for private domestic leagues
explanation: NSDF was created by MYAS in 1998 to channel public/private contributions (matching government grants) to fund special training for elite athletes (including TOPS) and develop specialized sports infrastructure.

topic: Olympic, Asian and Paralympic major competitions
subtopic: International games, venues and Olympic governance
text: Under the National Sports Development Code of India (2011), what is the age limit for holding an executive office-bearer post (President, Secretary General, Treasurer) in a National Sports Federation?
options: The maximum office-holder age is 45 years across all sports
Executive office-bearers may not exceed the maximum age of 70 years
No age limit exists; office bearers can hold lifelong office until 100 years of age
Minimum age of 65 years required before being eligible to hold executive office
explanation: The 2011 Sports Code imposes a strict age ceiling of 70 years for all executive office-bearers of National Sports Federations (NSFs) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Sports Authority of India and national schemes
text: In the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) framework at Sports Authority of India (SAI) training centers, what is the mandatory composition of the 'Internal Complaints Committee' (ICC)?
options: Composed entirely of male international coaches with zero female representation
Composed exclusively of active adolescent athletes under 15 years of age
The ICC has a senior woman chair, at least half women, and an external NGO member
Chaired by a commercial marketing representative from a private sports sponsor
explanation: The Internal Committee includes a senior woman Presiding Officer, at least half women members, and an external member meeting the statutory qualifications. The external member need not be described narrowly as coming from an NGO.

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Sports Authority of India and national schemes
text: Under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS), what monthly Out-of-Pocket Allowance (OPA) is provided to Core Group athletes by the Sports Authority of India?
options: TOPS athletes do not receive any monthly allowance during the 12-month cycle
₹10,00,000 per week deposited directly into commercial overseas equity funds
₹5,000 per year paid at the end of the Olympic cycle to selected athletes
TOPS provides ₹50,000 monthly as an out-of-pocket allowance.
explanation: Core Group athletes under TOPS receive a monthly Out-of-Pocket Allowance (OPA) of ₹50,000 to cover daily miscellaneous and personal expenses, in addition to full funding for customized training, equipment, and coaching.

topic: Olympic, Asian and Paralympic major competitions
subtopic: International games, venues and Olympic governance
text: Under the National Sports Development Code of India (2011), what transparency requirement applied to National Sports Federations?
options: Federations are exempt from maintaining accounting books or undergoing annual financial audits
Federations must publish audited annual accounts on their official websites.
Keeping all financial transactions and bank accounts strictly confidential from the public
Submitting financial records only once every 50 years to international governing bodies
explanation: Under the 2011 Code, NSFs were expected to maintain audited accounts and publish financial information proactively. This should be labelled as the historical 2011 framework because later governance legislation changed the regulatory context.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the World Anti-Doping Code, what is the 'Therapeutic Use Exemption' (TUE) granting process for athletes who have legitimate diagnosed medical conditions requiring a prohibited substance?
options: A TUE requires independent medical evidence showing necessity without extra performance benefit.
Athletes with medical conditions are completely barred from participating in competitive sports
Purchasing an over-the-counter exemption certificate from a private commercial pharmacy
Verbally informing the team physiotherapist in the locker room 5 minutes before the competition
explanation: Under WADA International Standard for TUE (ISTUE), an athlete must apply to their NADO/IF TUEC with documented medical evidence demonstrating that the prohibited substance is essential to treat a diagnosed condition and returns them to a normal health state without unfair enhancement.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: In Anti-Doping sample collection, what is the minimum specific gravity threshold required for a urine sample to be deemed valid for laboratory analysis under WADA guidelines?
options: Specific Gravity < 1.001 indicating pure distilled water without any dissolved solutes
Urine specific gravity is never measured during 1 doping-control collection
Specific Gravity must be exactly 2.500 across all collected athlete samples
Validity requires specific gravity ≥1.005, or ≥1.003 by digital refractometer.
explanation: Under WADA ISTI guidelines, a urine sample must have a specific gravity of at least 1.005 (or 1.003 if volume ≥ 150 mL via refractometer). If dilute, the DCO must collect additional samples until a suitable specimen is provided.

topic: Olympic, Asian and Paralympic major competitions
subtopic: International games, venues and Olympic governance

options: Miami, Florida, United States
Chicago, Illinois, United States
New York City, New York, United States
Los Angeles will host the Olympic Games.
explanation: The 2028 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games will be hosted by Los Angeles, California, USA (LA 2028).

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Sports Authority of India and national schemes
text: In the governance of Indian sports, what is the role of the 'Sports Authority of India' (SAI) established in 1984?
options: An international airline company that transports sports tourists across continents
A private commercial corporation that manufactures sports footwear for retail export
SAI supports talent scouting, national training centers, sports science, and coaching camps.
A sovereign judicial court that passes criminal sentences on international athletes
explanation: SAI is the premier sports development body under MYAS, managing 10 regional centres, NCOEs, national stadiums, high-performance sports science support, and national coaching camps.

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Sports Authority of India and national schemes
text: Under the National Sports Awards scheme of India, the 'Dronacharya Award' is conferred on:
options: It honors coaches who guide athletes or teams to outstanding international results.
Corporate business executives who sponsor commercial sports advertisements
Active junior athletes who have won medals at school national championships
Sports journalists who write match reports in national newspapers
explanation: The Dronacharya Award (instituted in 1985) is India's highest coaching honor, recognizing coaches for outstanding work on a consistent basis and enabling sportspersons to excel in international events.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the National Doping Control Regulations, what is the composition and function of the 'Anti-Doping Disciplinary Panel' (ADDP)?
options: A security branch that patrols sports hostel dormitories at night
A laboratory team that analyzes blood samples with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
A marketing committee that designs posters for anti-doping awareness campaigns
It is a legal, medical, and sport panel that hears ADRV cases and issues verdicts.
explanation: The ADDP is a quasi-judicial disciplinary body with legal, medical, and sport expertise. Its decisions are subject to the applicable appeal process and should not be described as immune from appeal.

topic: sports governance ethics and age verification
subtopic: National Sports Development Code and athlete safeguarding
text: Under the 'Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations' (MYAS), what financial support is provided for international exposure of national teams?
options: Athletes must pay 100% of all international travel and hotel expenses from personal savings
Approved teams receive funded travel, lodging, allowances, visas, and medical insurance.
Financial assistance is restricted strictly to domestic train travel within India
Commercial airline tickets are provided only if the team wins a gold medal in the final
explanation: Under the Scheme of Assistance to NSFs, the Government of India provides 100% financial assistance for preparing national teams, including international exposure, boarding/lodging, foreign coaches, and medical insurance.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the 2021 World Anti-Doping Code, what constitutes an 'Adverse Analytical Finding' (AAF)?
options: A medical report confirming that an athlete is physically fit to compete in the Olympics
It is a WADA laboratory report identifying a prohibited substance, metabolite, or marker.
A receipt confirming payment of annual federation membership fees
A laboratory finding indicating that the collected urine sample is 100% clean and negative
explanation: An Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) is the official analytical determination by a WADA-accredited laboratory confirming the presence of a prohibited substance, metabolite, or marker in Sample A.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the WADA Prohibited List, in which category are 'Glucocorticoids' classified and when are they prohibited?
options: Category P1; prohibited only in archery and shooting competitions
S9 glucocorticoids are prohibited in competition by injection, oral, or rectal routes.
Glucocorticoids are completely permitted at all times via all 4 administration routes
Category S1, anabolic agents, prohibited at all times by any route
explanation: Under WADA S9, all glucocorticoids are prohibited in-competition when administered by any injectable (intra-articular, intramuscular, periarticular), oral, or rectal route, requiring strict clearance wash-out periods or TUEs.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: In Anti-Doping sample collection, what is the role of the 'Doping Control Officer' (DCO)?
options: A commercial coach who prescribes tactical drills to the opposing sports squad
A sports journalist who broadcasts live video of athlete testing sessions
The DCO manages collection, chain of custody, and athlete rights at the testing session.
A pharmacist who dispenses ergogenic performance supplements to national squads
explanation: The DCO is the certified official responsible for managing sample collection, verifying athlete identity, overseeing direct observation of urine provision (or blood draw via BCO), and securing sealed transport to WADA-accredited labs.

topic: Olympic, Asian and Paralympic major competitions
subtopic: International games, venues and Olympic governance
text: Which city will host the XXXIII Olympic Summer Games in 2024?
options: Madrid, Spain
London, United Kingdom
Paris, France
Berlin, Germany
explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games were hosted by Paris, France (Paris 2024).

topic: Olympic, Asian and Paralympic major competitions

A commercial construction company that builds shopping malls in New Delhi
The IOA is India's National Olympic Committee for managing delegations at major Games.
A private medical hospital providing open-heart surgery for retired politicians
explanation: The IOA is the recognized National Olympic Committee (NOC) and Commonwealth Games Association (CGA) for India, managing Indian representation and team participation in multi-sport mega games.

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Sports Authority of India and national schemes
text: Under the National Sports Awards scheme of India, the 'Arjuna Award' is conferred for:

It recognizes sustained international performance, leadership, and sportsmanship.
Lifetime contribution to sports journalism across regional television channels
Winning a gold medal in an inter-school friendly match after 4 seasons
explanation: The Arjuna Award (instituted in 1961) is conferred by the President of India to sportspersons for consistent high performance, sportsmanship, and discipline over the preceding four years.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA India) regulations, what is 'Results Management'?
options: Publishing athlete telephone numbers on public social media websites
Managing the ticket sales revenue generated by national championship events
Calculating the total points scored by an athlete in a basketball match
Results management covers ADRV notification, adjudication, sanctions, and appeals.
explanation: Results Management encompasses the pre-hearing review, initial notice, provisional suspension, investigation, disciplinary panel adjudication (ADDP), and appeals (NADAP/CAS) under the International Standard for Results Management (ISRM).

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Sports Authority of India and national schemes
text: Under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS), what is the 'Development Group' instituted by the Sports Authority of India?
options: TOPS group for emerging athletes with future medal potential and support toward the Core Group
The TOPS Core Group for athletes already identified as immediate medal prospects
The Mission Olympic Cell that reviews nominations and sanctions individualized support
An SAI excellence center providing general coaching rather than a TOPS athlete category
explanation: The TOPS Development Group supports emerging or junior athletes who have longer-term Olympic or Paralympic medal potential, with customized training and competition support as they develop toward the Core Group.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the World Anti-Doping Code, what constitutes an 'Anti-Doping Rule Violation' (ADRV) under Article 2.5 regarding Tampering or Attempted Tampering with any part of Doping Control?
options: Conduct that subverts doping control or compromises sample integrity
Requesting a copy of the completed Doping Control Form through normal procedure
Politely requesting an additional sealed bottle of drinking water
Arriving early at a scheduled doping-control collection station
explanation: Article 2.5 (Tampering) encompasses fraudulent actions intended to disrupt, alter, or subvert the doping control process (e.g., sample substitution, chemical adulteration, falsifying records), carrying a standard 4-year ban.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: Under the WADA Prohibited List, in which category are 'Peptide Hormones, Growth Factors, Related Substances, and Mimetics' (e.g., Erythropoietin, Human Growth Hormone, IGF-1) classified?
options: Category S6 for stimulants, prohibited during competition only
Category P1 for beta-blockers, prohibited in archery only
Category M2 for mechanical manipulation of blood
Category S2 peptide hormones, prohibited at all times
explanation: WADA Category S2 includes peptide hormones (EPO, hGH, GHRHs, IGF-1), which are strictly prohibited at all times (both in- and out-of-competition) via all routes due to potent systemic anabolic and erythropoietic actions.

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations
subtopic: Anti-doping rules, testing and compliance
text: In the Anti-Doping analytical process, what is the role of 'Gas Chromatography-Combustion-Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometry' (GC-C-IRMS)?
options: A test detecting viral antibodies in saliva samples during international travel
A test measuring calcium mineral density in the lumbar vertebrae
A test measuring resting blood glucose and hemoglobin concentrations
GC-C-IRMS distinguishes endogenous from synthetic steroids by carbon-isotope ratio
explanation: GC-C-IRMS is the confirmatory gold standard method used to distinguish synthetic exogenous testosterone from endogenous natural testosterone based on differences in ¹³C/¹²C isotopic signatures.

topic: Olympic, Asian and Paralympic major competitions

options: Rome and Florence, Italy
Milano and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy

NCOE Kolkata, West Bengal, is a high-performance center for elite archery and gymnastics
NSNIS Patiala is SAI's institute for coach education, sports science, and high-performance training
NCOE Sonepat, Haryana, is a high-performance center for elite wrestling and judo

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards

text: Under the National Sports Awards scheme of India, the 'Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy' is awarded annually to:

The state sports council that constructs the largest public stadium
The corporate company that donates the most money to sports charities
The best individual track-and-field sprinter at the national championship

topic: anti-doping awareness and WADA/NADA regulations

options: A private, non-governmental commercial club operating without government oversight
A statutory autonomous body with a government-appointed Director General
A subsidiary company of an international private sports footwear brand
A division of the Indian Armed Forces dedicated to mountain rescue

This item is anchored to the enacted Act text; as of the notification date, the NADA Rules 2021 remained the operative rules.

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards

To build commercial fitness facilities in private corporate offices across urban cities
To conduct annual recreational sports leagues exclusively for retired administrators
To manufacture all athletic apparel and equipment domestically for commercial export
explanation: The KISCE initiative under the Khelo India scheme aims to upgrade one existing sports training facility in each State and Union Territory into a world-class training center equipped with top sports science and coaching support.

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards

options: The National Sports Tribunal (NST)
The Mission Olympic Cell (MOC)
The Union Public Commission (UPC)
The Central Vigilance Wing (CVW)
explanation: The Mission Olympic Cell (MOC) within the Sports Authority of India (SAI) comprises eminent sports personalities, administrators, and high-performance experts tasked with evaluating athlete performance and approving TOPS funding and training support.

topic: Anti-doping governance and WADA Prohibited List

text: Under the WADA Prohibited List (in force as of January 2026), what substance category is classified under Class S1?
options: Peptide Hormones and Growth Factors
Beta-2 Agonists and Bronchodilators
Anabolic Androgenic Steroids and Agents
Hormone and Metabolic Modulator Drugs
explanation: Class S1 is the Anabolic Agents category, which includes anabolic androgenic steroids (AAS) and related agents.

topic: Anti-doping governance and WADA Prohibited List
subtopic: NADA Whereabouts filing failures and Anti-Doping Rule Violations
text: Under National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) regulations, how many Whereabouts Failures (Filing Failures or Missed Tests) within a 12-month period constitute an Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV)?
options: Any single (1) missed test or filing failure in 12 months
Any combination of six (6) missed tests or filing failures in 12 months
Any combination of eight (8) missed tests or filing failures in 12 months
Any combination of three (3) missed tests or filing failures in 12 months
explanation: Under Article 2.4 of the WADA / NADA Code, any combination of three (3) Whereabouts Failures (Filing Failures and/or Missed Tests) within a rolling 12-month period by an athlete in a Registered Testing Pool (RTP) constitutes an ADRV.

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards

Outstanding performance over the preceding four (4) years

topic: Sports governance ethics and National Sports Development Code

Maximum age limit of 75 years
Maximum age limit of 80 years
Maximum age limit of 70 years

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards

One-time cash prize reward of Rs 50,000 for winning 1 school medal
Monthly training stipend of Rs 10,000 per month for up to 2 years
Lifetime pension grant of Rs 1 lakh per month starting from 18 years

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) Core vs Development allowance
text: Under India's Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS), what is the monthly Out-of-Pocket Allowance (OPA) provided to athletes selected in the TOPS 'Core Group'?

Rs 50,000 per month out-of-pocket allowance
Rs 1,50,000 per month out-of-pocket allowance
Rs 3,00,000 per month out-of-pocket allowance

topic: Anti-doping governance and WADA Prohibited List
subtopic: WADA Class S3 Beta-2 Agonists permitted inhaled thresholds
text: Under the WADA Prohibited List (in force as of January 2026), what is the maximum permitted 24-hour inhaled dose for Salbutamol without requiring a TUE?

A maximum inhaled dose of 5000 micrograms in 24 hours
A maximum inhaled dose of 1600 micrograms in 24 hours
A maximum inhaled dose of 0 micrograms in 24 hours; therefore prohibited
explanation: Inhaled salbutamol is permitted under WADA rules up to a maximum of 1600 micrograms over 24 hours in divided doses not to exceed 600 micrograms over any 8-hour period; higher doses require a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE).

topic: Anti-doping governance and WADA Prohibited List

The Sports Authority of India Governing Body
The Indian Olympic Association Council
The National Anti-Doping Disciplinary Panel

107 total medals (28 Gold, 38 Silver, 41 Bronze)
125 total medals (35 Gold, 45 Silver, 45 Bronze)
150 total medals (50 Gold, 50 Silver, 50 Bronze)

topic: Indian sports schemes and National Sports Awards
subtopic: Dronacharya Award cash rewards and categories

Rs 25 lakh cash reward
Rs 15 lakh cash reward
Rs 50 lakh cash reward

topic: Sports governance ethics and National Sports Development Code
subtopic: National Sports Development Code of India (2011) cooling-off period
text: Under the National Sports Development Code of India (2011), what cooling-off period is mandatory for a Secretary General or Treasurer after serving two consecutive terms of 4 years each?

Cooling-off period of at least eight years after two consecutive terms
No cooling-off period required under the National Sports Development Code
Cooling-off period of at least four years after two consecutive terms
explanation: Under the Sports Code 2011, the Secretary General/Treasurer may serve a maximum of two consecutive terms of 4 years each (8 years), after which a mandatory cooling-off period of at least 4 years (one term) must lapse before re-election.
